title: inotify event structure
summary: An inotify event returned by read(2) on an inotify file descriptor: wd (watch descriptor), mask (event mask), cookie (for rename pairing), len (length of the name field), then a NUL-terminated filename (if the watched path is a directory).

ext.summary: An inotify event returned by read(2) on an inotify file descriptor: wd (watch descriptor), mask (event mask), cookie (for rename pairing), len (length of the name field), then a NUL-terminated filename (if the watched path is a directory).

structure.meaning: Event mask: IN_ACCESS, IN_MODIFY, IN_ATTRIB, IN_CLOSE_WRITE, IN_CLOSE_NOWRITE, IN_OPEN, IN_MOVED_FROM, IN_MOVED_TO, IN_CREATE, IN_DELETE, IN_DELETE_SELF, IN_MOVE_SELF, IN_UNMOUNT, IN_Q_OVERFLOW, IN_IGNORED.
Cookie for pairing IN_MOVED_FROM and IN_MOVED_TO events.
Length of the name field (including NUL padding to sizeof(struct inotify_event) + len).
Filename (NUL-terminated, padded to 4-byte alignment). Present only if the watched path is a directory.

ext.example_decoded: inotify event: wd 1, mask IN_CREATE (0x00000100), cookie 0, len 8, name 'foo'
notes: Multiple events can be read in a single read(2) call.
IN_Q_OVERFLOW indicates events were dropped due to queue overflow.
inotify does not recurse into subdirectories; each directory needs its own watch.
fanotify is the newer, more powerful alternative (mount/fs notifications, permission events).
